assessment_summary.before: Art. 35 frac. XIX of the SS Interior Regulation explicitly designates the DGE as the RSI National Focal Point and assigns IHR Article 4 duties. Actor fit is strong. Procedure fit is partial: 24-hour availability, internal contact lists, and WHO communication protocols are not codified. Coordination with SRE (DGRI) and COFEPRIS is implied but not operationally specified.
assessment_summary.after: This provision forms part of the preliminary mapping for IHR-OBL-001. A conclusion that procedures are absent is not supported by this provision alone: NOM-017 §§6.6.3–6.6.4 assigns inter-level duties and refers to the IHR and an international surveillance manual; §8.1.4 defines a domestic immediate-notification chain. The scope of these provisions for this specific obligation and the referred manual remain to be reviewed.

audit_note.after: AUD-NOM-017: absence claim withheld; referral and domestic procedure located. This does not establish complete implementation. Instrument is a regulation, not a statute.

assessment_summary.before: NOM-017 numeral 6.6.1-6.6.2 reiterates and operationalises the DGE NFP designation at the technical-normative level, confirming DGE as the domestic focal point for PHEIC notifications. Provides operational specificity not found in the Reglamento Interior, but does not fully specify 24-hour communication protocols or backup NFP contacts.
assessment_summary.after: This provision forms part of the preliminary mapping for IHR-OBL-001. A conclusion that procedures are absent is not supported by this provision alone: NOM-017 §§6.6.3–6.6.4 assigns inter-level duties and refers to the IHR and an international surveillance manual; §8.1.4 defines a domestic immediate-notification chain. The scope of these provisions for this specific obligation and the referred manual remain to be reviewed.

audit_note.after: AUD-NOM-017: absence claim withheld; referral and domestic procedure located. This does not establish complete implementation.

assessment_summary.before: Art. 2 establishes DGE as a deconcentrated administrative unit of SS, providing the institutional-structural basis for the NFP designation in Art. 35. Anchoring is actor-level only; no IHR obligations or procedures are specified here.
assessment_summary.after: This provision forms part of the preliminary mapping for IHR-OBL-001. audit_note.after: AUD-NOM-017: absence claim withheld; referral and domestic procedure located. This does not establish complete implementation.

assessment_summary.before: Art. 134 establishes the SINAVE and assigns SS the mandate to develop epidemiological surveillance capacity at all levels. Fourteen fracciones cover detection, notification, laboratory confirmation, and information management. Does not explicitly reference IHR Annex 1 benchmarks or time-bound development milestones.
assessment_summary.after: Article 133(II), not Article 134, assigns the Health Ministry responsibility to establish and operate SINAVE. Article 134 separately covers surveillance, prevention and control of listed diseases. These provisions must be read with NOM-017 and relevant implementing documents before assessing the whole IHR obligation.

audit_note.after: AUD-LGS-133: incorrect article attribution corrected; no new compliance score assigned.
Instrument is a regulation, not a statute.

assessment_summary.after: This provision forms part of the preliminary mapping for IHR-OBL-003. assessment_summary.before: Art. 9 RLGS lists required maritime health documentation and governs its use at designated ports, partially anchoring the Art. 37 Maritime Declaration of Health obligation. assessment_summary.after: Article 31 specifies who must present the maritime health declaration to the Health Ministry on arrival and refers to the form established by the IHR. audit_note.after: AUD-DECLARATIONS: responsible person, arrival trigger and form reference located; complete compliance not determined.

assessment_summary.before: Art. 9 RLGS governs aviation health documentation at designated international airports, partially anchoring Art. 38 Aircraft General Declaration requirements. assessment_summary.after: Article 30 specifies who must present the aircraft health declaration to the Health Ministry on arrival and refers to the form established by the IHR. audit_note.after: AUD-DECLARATIONS: responsible person, arrival trigger and form reference located; complete compliance not determined.

assessment_summary.before: No domestic provision found that specifically prohibits charging travellers for personal health measures (examination, vaccination, prophylaxis, health documents) required under IHR Art. 40. The corpus does not contain a traveller health measures fee framework.
assessment_summary.after: Article 7 provides a general gratuity rule for international health services and documents, with exceptions. A relevant domestic provision is therefore identified. Its coverage and fee exceptions must be assessed against IHR Art. 40 and fiscal provisions before assigning an anchoring or compliance conclusion.

after.provision_text: 8.1.4 La notificación inmediata de los padecimientos, condiciones, eventos o urgencia epidemiológicas emergentes o reemergentes se realiza por las unidades de vigilancia epidemiológica o sus equivalentes en cada uno de los niveles técnico-administrativos hasta la DGE antes de que transcurran 24 horas de su conocimiento por el procedimiento de notificación establecido vía telefónica, fax o medio electrónico.
after.topic: Immediate domestic reporting at technical-administrative levels
after.actor_mentioned: Epidemiological surveillance units or equivalents at each technical-administrative level; DGE
after.duty_created: Immediate notification by surveillance units or equivalents at the technical-administrative levels up to DGE, before 24 hours from knowledge.
after.procedure_created: Knowledge-based domestic notification deadline; telephone, fax or electronic means.
after.coordination_mechanism: Multi-level reporting up to DGE; the final text does not use the draft wording successive superior levels.
after.relevance_to_ihr: The final NOM-017 section 8.1.4 requires epidemiological surveillance units or their equivalents at the different technical-administrative levels to notify up to DGE before 24 hours from knowledge of the event, by telephone, fax or electronic means. This is not a finding of a direct exchange from every unit to DGE. The IHR Article 6 deadline instead runs from assessment.
